patch.value: GH-764: one host-global flag collision quarantines an entire extension and suggests reinstalling the installed package

Extension activation rejects one command flag that shadows a host global by dropping every otherwise-valid command in the package. Unknown-command recovery then recommends installing the package even though the activation failure proves it is already installed, and bundled aliases may resolve that suggestion to a different package.

The integrity decision between per-command quarantine and atomic extension activation is documented; diagnostics state the chosen blast radius; unknown-command recovery suppresses generic install advice when a matching activation failure exists; installed package identity is preserved; multi-command extension, bundled-alias, doctor, packed-package, and token-efficient error-envelope tests pass.

A command-level contract failure has an explicit bounded blast radius, healthy commands remain usable when safe, and recovery points to the known activation failure without suggesting installation of an installed package.

One invalid --json declaration removes the extension's complete command surface; the resulting unknown-command response recommends pm install for an already-installed and potentially alias-colliding package.
